idiom_name: Try/Option with recover and getOrElse; Pekko CircuitBreaker for call protection
implementation_notes: Scala's Try (Success/Failure) is the fallback combinator: recover and recoverWith supply the substitute, getOrElse the simple default, and Future.recover the asynchronous case, so the degraded value is produced by a function rather than a mode machine. Pekko's CircuitBreaker documents the other half - it fails fast and, in the documentation's own terms, lets you serve cached content while the breaker is open - so the common Scala stack is the breaker for detection plus Try/Either for substitution. Only non-fatal exceptions are caught by Try (NonFatal), which is the right default for dependency failures.
code_sketch:
val report: Report =
  Try(backend.report(id))
    .recover { case e: TimeoutException =>
      metrics.degraded(e)
      Cache.report(id)                 // stale, but useful
    }
    .getOrElse(Report.placeholder)
pitfalls: Try and recover catch NonFatal, which includes most runtime bugs: pattern-match the dependency's exception types instead of a catch-all recover.
A blocking substitute inside Future.recover runs on the execution context and can starve it - mark blocking code explicitly.
getOrElse is by-name, but recoverWith and orElse re-run whole computations: keep whatever they retry idempotent.
